name: ColorSwatch
requestedBy: agent (splitting the docs-parts batch, on the owner's instruction to work the pending requests)
need: A colour is a value a person picks, and the system has no control for picking one. `<input type="color">` is exactly the raw control lint-rules refuses, so the one place that needs it — the site's own settings panel, where a visitor tries the system in another brand — is five hand-rolled buttons carrying a written exception. Filed as its own record because the batch it arrived in was about documentation parts and this is not one: Code and Prose render text, this one takes input.

consideredAlternatives.whyNot: The native picker cannot be styled, opens an OS dialog that owes the system nothing, and is the raw control the linter refuses everywhere else.

The right SEMANTICS for a closed set of brands, and the settings panel should use them. What is missing underneath is the swatch itself: a colour rendered as a control-sized target that reads on any surface, including one its own colour matches.
A badge states a value; it is not a target and carries no selected state.

It is the status quo and it is written down as an exception, which is the honest version of "nobody decided". The second consumer is the trigger, and a brand picker is the kind of thing every product that themes gets asked for.

proposedApi: value (a CSS colour), label (required — a colour cannot be its own name to a screen reader), selected, onSelect, size (sm | md). Draws its own edge from --border rather than from the colour, so a swatch the colour of the surface is still a visible target.
sources: Measured on the site's settings panel, 2026-08-23: five buttons, 31 lines of CSS, one written exception. Primer, Polaris and Carbon each ship a swatch or colour-input primitive.
decision: Approved and built 2026-08-26, the day it was split out. The settings panel gave back 24 lines of CSS and the written exception for a raw control. `label` is REQUIRED, which is the decision inside the decision: a colour has no accessible name of its own, so a swatch without one is a button that reads as "button" to anyone not looking at it. The dot draws its own edge from --border rather than from the value, so a swatch the colour of the surface is still a target — the case a colour-as-background approach gets wrong exactly when it matters. Its own doc block cost a linter fix: the raw-control rule read the sentence naming `<input type="color">` as a violation, and six sibling rules had the same hole (fixed the same day).
decidedBy: owner (2026-08-26, told the pending requests to be worked)
